title.value: Minimax and Neyman–Pearson Meta-Learning for Outlier Languages
title.justification: The title is explicitly mentioned at the end of the paper's details and also in the arXiv reference.
title.quote: Minimax and Neyman–Pearson Meta-Learning for Outlier Languages

analysis.description: This paper proposes two variants of Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML) for addressing issues in cross-lingual NLP, focusing on outlier languages that are often not well represented during training. The two variants, Minimax MAML and Neyman–Pearson MAML, are designed to be robust to uncertain language distributions and aim to improve performance in zero- and few-shot settings. The paper also introduces a new adaptive optimizer to approximate Nash equilibrium in these settings.

type.justification: The paper primarily deals with theoretical frameworks and introduces new criteria for meta-learning (Minimax and Neyman–Pearson) in decision theory, reframing the MAML approach for outlier languages in cross-lingual NLP.
type.quote: In this work, we interpret meta-learning within a decision-theoretic framework (Bickel and Doksum, 2015).

name.justification: The paper addresses cross-lingual Natural Language Processing tasks, specifically part-of-speech tagging and question answering, which are core NLP tasks.
name.quote: We evaluate both model variants on two popular NLP tasks, part-of-speech tagging and question answering.

name.justification: The paper is focused on transferring knowledge between resource-rich and resource-poor languages, a fundamental aspect of cross-lingual transfer learning.
name.quote: MAML has come to the fore as a promising paradigm: it explicitly trains neural models that adapt to new languages quickly by extrapolating from just a few annotated data points.

name.justification: The research extends the model-agnostic meta-learning strategy by proposing the Minimax and Neyman–Pearson variants which are key components of meta-learning.
name.quote: Model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML) has been recently put forth as a strategy to learn resource-poor languages in a sample-efficient fashion.

name.justification: The paper bases its research on refining the MAML strategy and compares its variants against the standard MAML approach.
name.quote: Model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML) has been recently put forth as a strategy to learn resource-poor languages in a sample-efficient fashion.

is_contributed.justification: MAML itself is not a contribution of the paper, but is the baseline model the paper aims to improve upon with its proposed variants.
is_contributed.quote: MAML, we show, minimises the expected risk across languages found in the training distribution.

is_executed.justification: The paper conducts experiments using MAML for comparison against its proposed approaches, indicating it was executed.
is_executed.quote: We report gains for their average and minimum performance across low-resource languages in zero- and few-shot settings, compared to joint multi-source transfer and vanilla MAML.

is_compared.justification: MAML is used as a baseline for comparison with the proposed Minimax and Neyman-Pearson MAML models.
is_compared.quote: We report gains for their average and minimum performance across low-resource languages in zero- and few-shot settings, compared to joint multi-source transfer and vanilla MAML.
